module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Maximality of $k = 43$ with restricted digit counts in bases $3 \le b < k$

Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.

The sequence Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.

*References:*
- [A306424](https://oeis.org/A306424)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA306424


open List Finset Nat

/--
Numbers $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.
-/
def Condition (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  -- The bases $b$ range over $3 \le b \le k-1$, expressed as $3 \le b$ and $b < k$.
  ∀ b : ℕ, 3 ≤ b ∧ b < k → ((Nat.digits b k).toFinset.card) ≤ 2

/--
The $n$-th number $k$ such that the base $b$ expansion of $k$ for each
$b = 3..k-1$ never contains more than two distinct digits.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ := n.nth Condition


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_2 : a 2 = 2 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 3 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by sorry

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 5 := by sorry


/--
Conjecture: The sequence is finite, with 43 being the last term.

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/306424.wip.lean#L276"]
theorem forty_three_is_max : Condition 43 ∧ ∀ k : ℕ, 43 < k → ¬Condition k := by
    sorry

end OeisA306424

reformulations.difference: OEIS lists positive solutions with offset 1, whereas Lean uses zero-indexed Nat.nth on Condition, which also holds vacuously at 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Zero is exactly the extra element preceding the positive solutions, so these two indexing conventions cancel. In scratch Lean I proved, for every n, `a (n + 1) = Nat.nth (fun k => 0 < k ∧ Condition k) n`, including Nat.nth's default-zero behavior after a finite enumeration is exhausted. Thus every defined OEIS index has the intended value. The additional value a 0 = 0 and the default tail are not used by any claim about OEIS terms; admitting 0 also cannot change whether 43 is the largest solution.

review.notes: All eight declarations were checked. Independent Lean proofs verified the five initial-value tests, Condition 43, failure at 44, and equivalence of the maximum statement with a finite positive solution set having last term 43. Computation matched all 23 listed positive terms and found no additional solutions below 1000. The research-solved tag agrees with OEIS's June 1, 2026 proof record and the cited literature. The historical proof artifact states the identical claim and contains no explicit sorry or custom axioms; its attempted replay after import remapping encountered compatibility errors under the current toolchain, so I do not claim a full kernel replay of that artifact. This does not reveal a statement or status discrepancy.
